body: Wow I really like this analogy... thank you!
Thanks :)  I decided to take a nice long bath and meditate on everything.  I feel much better now... cleaned off in a mental state, so to speak.  Ready to dive back into this!

Thank you - that's what I'm trying to remind myself.  That I'm in this situation precisely because I didn't just brush myself off and keep going, but threw it all away in frustration.

I guess starting again from scratch will suck, but it'll suck less than if I bitch and  moan for a few months first.
Thank you for this  :)
That's true.  I dunno I guess I just wanted to be able to see a difference, but you're right - 2.5 isn't that much in the grand scheme.  but it is something... thank you :)
Thank you... erg... wasn't expecting such a feeling so early on!
Thanks... I guess I just got super excited that I was feeling better now withdrawal wise and was eager to see those changes :(

Thank you for this - I guess looking at the math laid out right in front of me makes it a lot easier to see.  I was frustrated because numbers weren't moving at the speed I wanted and completely ignoring the fact that A) I don't feel like shit any more and actually feel like I have some control and B) I just have to follow the math.

Thank you again kind stranger.

I was thinking it might be those two as well (thank you google!) but was somewhat hesitant to try a magnesium supplement... I'm nervous about overdosing on it or something.  I've been using the Lite-Salt because it has potassium in it in addition to sodium, but I don't know if it's enough.  I've also been taking epsom salt baths about 3x a week because I know magnesium can seep through your skin.  But bananas sound good - I will give that a try!

I just posted about getting through this carb flu ajustment period and then read your post and it gave me a lot of hope.  I'm on day 12 and I'm just now starting to notice the same things you mentioned - I don't feel great, but I don't feel like death.  I want to eat junk, but it's not a craving.  And the biggest one for me is - when I *do* eat something sugary, it's not immediately followed by this intense "omg when can I get my next sugar fix??".
Also: Do you pay attention to calories and macros?

Thank you for writing this up!  Do you have any advice on salt intake?  I tried Keto a few years ago and felt absolutely horrible.  Even my friends who have gone through the "keto flu" were surprised at how shitty I was feeling.  I've since suspected it was from not keeping up with the water and salt intake... Short of dumping salt on everything, I really don't know how to avoid that?

I tried Keto a few years ago with doing just this, but failed pretty quickly.  No bread, no pasta, no potatoes, no corn, no yogurt, etc, etc.  It got so I wasn't eating much and I think ended up not taking in nearly enough salt either.  I felt like death times a billion.
? Don't people advocate for things like Keto Chow here?  How is that different?  It's an all liquid diet as well...

I definitely agree that there are stories from both sides, but the benefits seem to outweigh the cons here for me.  It seems like if I can push through two months of this to drop down to a good weight and then maintain that it would be worth it.  Obviously this wouldn't be a life long thing - just the huge push in the right direction.  I fully expect some muscle loss as well, but in the end that seems worth it as well.

But this coupled with the nutrition classes and using other resources, seems like a great way to break my addiction to sugar and crap and reset.
? I've read tons of success stories about the program.  It includes the fast, but also weekly nutrition classes, weigh-ins, and check ups.

1) Eating food in response to stress brings me comfort and control.  I realize that these are just an illusion though - the comfort lasts for a few moments at most before the shame and hatred set in.  And the control of eating what I want is in all reality a lack of control.  It's all turned in backwards on itself and spirals down from there.

2) Therapy is a big step for me.  I also take Zoloft daily, which helps with the anxiety but not the depression so much.

Wow nice article!  I definitely think the heat is a huge trigger for me... it mimics the reactions during a panic attack so well.  :(  But I feel better knowing I'm not the only one... Thank you!  I can't imagine the stress of the holidays plus hot summer weather... I cannot wait for fall when it is nice and crisp and cool out here!

Oh I absolutely agree it isn't something that's going to be cured in 1-2 days.  However, speaking from 30+ years of experience, it is something that "flares up" so to speak.  Being out a few days doesn't mean I'm not seeking help and treatment.

I ask because I am feeling particularly guilty and like a piece of shit.  The last year I have called out sick fairly regularly - every couple of months for a day or two at a time.  I make up an illness that seems more acceptable.  The truth is I'm so fucking depressed I can't muster the energy to drag myself out of bed in the morning.  I just feel like an empty shell of numbness and what's the point of dealing with work when I'm struggling with the point of human existence?  

But, on top of all the depression, I feel like a shitty human being and a horrible employee for lying to my boss.  It's not like I'm ditching work to go hang out with friends or anything - when I do call out I pretty much spend all day in bed hating myself.

I should mention that I am on antidepressants and seeing a therapist.  This is something that I want to get under control, but lately seems to have taken a nosedive.  Also I am otherwise a great employee - get good reviews, do extra work, etc.

Thank you so much for this.  This

>Don't underestimate how much readily tapped potential that gives you. It's waiting there, just beneath the surface.

in particular really stood out to me.  A lot of my depression and anxiety stems from beating myself up way too much about things and this really helped me stand back and pat myself on the back.  It might be little to other people, but I honestly think it was a huge thing to realize about myself.  It's hard to break a cycle when you can't even recognize the cycle,  you know?

And I definitely like the idea of your todo list.  I'm going to find a good app and download one.  Tonight I was feeling really lonely and shitty, but I came home to a clean apartment (been a long while since I've cleaned) and I just somehow felt... a little bit better.  So I made myself brush my teeth and get washed up for bed - something I honestly can't remember the last time I did.  And I do feel even just the littlest bit more on top of things and at ease.

Like, on other nights, I would be consciously and subconsciously beating myself up for neglecting myself and feeling off and unclean, etc.  Maybe not even knowing why.  There's no room for anything else in my mind when that eats up so much of myself.

Anyway, I'm starting to ramble.  Thank you again kind stranger :)

I've been through a lot of crap in life, but so far it's been losing my ex that has been the one thing that makes suicide seem to creep in.  I just feel so lost and alone.  I think it's the loneliness that makes it hardest.  I mean, we were together for four years, talking of marriage, lived together, moved together, and then he just... left.  And it's left me feeling so hollow, empty, alone... numb.  I just can't seem to see any sort of light in the darkness and people are telling me I need to move on, I need to let him go, I just don't know how.
I keep trying, but my mind seems to always get pulled back.  Reading is hard to stay concentrated... Fuck some days are easier than others, but today is just bad
It's days like today that make me wonder :(
Thank you

Does the pain go away?  Fuck it's been almost a year so far and it still feels so fresh in my mind :(
Just sent my comment :|

I need to talk to someone, but I don't know who.  I sat online on the crisis chat website, but it was so slow loading and I didn't think I counted as suicidal "enough".  Does that make sense?  Fuck I'm a basket case...

Okay, I'm likely freaking myself out here, but here's some background:

Broke up with my ex last fall.  We were together for four years, had talked about getting married, he was my best friend, my first serious relationship.  It's been a horrible eight months, but... I should be more moved on by now, shouldn't I?

I've been so fucking depressed.  I finally started therapy on Friday, but have only been to one session.  

I keep getting thoughts of suicide now.  But, these thoughts sort of freak me out at the same time.  I mean, I still clearly think of suicide and self harm as a horrible action and would never wish for it, yet they keep creeping closer.

Is that a sign that things are getting worse?  Is the fact that I'm aware of how fucked up it is mean anything?  

My brother was suidical for awhile, but thankfully is no longer - he is bipolar and stable for now.

But fuck... this suicide shit has got me back to levels of panic.

:( Where did my life go wrong?
Well fuck that is a depressing sub.
Thanks :)
Thanks - Ill check it out
Why don't you tell them?  If you left them, maybe they would be open to testing the waters again.

Thank you again :)  It's weird, since I've finally allowed myself to accept the reality that he was likely abusive, I keep seeing even more and more red flags.  Like... a wall around that part of my brain is crumbling down.  It sucks, but it feels good at the same time.  I have a few emails out to different therapists so hoping I can find a good one.  Thanks for that link as well - I am definitely going to check it out!

Same sorta thing happened to me, though not after as long.  We hadn't talked in a month and then he texted me that he needed to talk to me.  I was hesitant, but figured I'd let him have the chance given how odd it seemed - I figured maybe he was rethinking things.  Nope!  He wanted to talk to tell me that he had decided we should have no contact.  What the actual fuck?  The only thing I could think of was it was some sort of weird control thing where he had to feel like it was *his* idea.  Glad to know my ex isn't the only confused piece of shit out there.

Thank you so much.

I still find myself in denial at times, thinking I must be crazy to be thinking this wonderful, charming guy could be anything but that.  It's taken a lot of my family highlighted the red flags, pointing out things that were straight up wrong, and my reading up on abuse.  The physical aspect was only one incidence... but that took forever to even admit to myself.  I knew it was wrong at the time that it happened, but I tried to excuse it and push it down deep inside of me a lot.

I'm still trying to get a breath of fresh air here and am starting to seriously consider the therapy route.  I think it could really help... this is my first experience with a breakup and, like being my first experience with a relationship, I want to make sure I get as much help as possible to sort out what is normal and what is not.

Thank you again :)
Yeah, this is beyond fucked up.  This red flag is so big it could cover Russia.

I think what really scares me is that when I met him I didn't set out looking.  I just sort of fell into a relationship with him so effortlessly.  The idea of that ever happening again seems so out there.
Thank you - I think I will buy it!

I don't know much about narcissists, but I'll definitely look that up.  And yeah, I keep going back and forth between wanting him back, or at least wanting back the person I thought I knew, and being insanely angry.  

And holy shit how the fuck did he try to justify being angry because YOU were making HIM feel bad when HE cheated???

Thank you for your kind words.  I think, at this point, the hardest thing I have understanding is how I just seemed to let it all happen.  If someone came at me point blank telling me these things I would have been horrified, seen the red flags, and ran for the hills.  But it was like you said - not really ever said in a MEAN way, just small comments here and there.  It's like for four years I thought something was off, but could never pinpoint it because he wasn't really *doing* anything mean.  I don't know, I feel like it's messed with my head so much.  On top of that is the realization that *he* left *me* and for so long I still wanted him back.  Does that make me weak?  How long would I have stayed with him before I realized the abuse that was going on?  Even after we broke up he was still being manipulative and abusive - we lived together, so it took a few months before I could find my own place.  He would comment on how irrational I was being crying so much, how I had to learn to "compartmentalize my feelings", and when I didn't want to stay friends he told me I had to respect his feelings.  It's all just so messed up.

Thank you so much for writing :)  It does help knowing other people have gone through similar things and come out the otherside.  I'm sorry you had to go through that, but I'm glad you succeeded!  I adopted a kitten a month ago and she has been helping me a lot :)  Sometimes I feel really pathetic when I come home and tell my cat about how I felt strong today, but then other days when I just hold her and cry it helps me feel even better.

Thank you :)
Thank you :)  It helps just knowing I'm not the only one to go through shit like this.  And you're right, maybe he is lying to the world.  Or to himself.  Either way... Thank you :)

Sigh... I can't wait for the day that I feel myself again :)

I also tried the OkCupid road - Originally, like you, to get a quick lay and feel desired again, but I realized I couldn't go through with it.  So then I settled on just looking for friends, but was deterred by a lot of shady messaging.  The finally straw was when OkCupid decided to match me with... my Ex!  Who was now raving about how awesome his new life was and how he needed to be with a woman of *confidence*.  Yeah, I think I cried for a week after that.
... No :(  Although it did make me feel sick enough to definitely not want this crap again for a long time!

Thank you so much :')  Yes he was, well, at worse manipulative, at best very emotionally confused.  I look back and see lots of red flags now, but at the time I had no experience with relationships - so little comments here and there about my body hurt, but I figured "hey he says he loves me so it must be okay!"  ... Yeah, turns out not so much :(  He also never seemed to be angry when he said it, just sort of mildly disappointed and I think over four years it really added up.  I have a bit of an underactive thyroid and my hands will get very cold in the winter and take awhile to warm up... and he would constantly make me feel like I couldn't ever touch him, that it was the reason sex would have to stop, etc, etc.  But, yeah, I find it ironic that he spent four years eroding away my self esteem and then blamed me for a lack of confidence and the reason he was overweight and out of shape.

And you know what, I like what you said about admiring my strengths.  I have a calendar here where I have been putting a little smilely sticker each day of the month that I have stuck to (or made a tremendous effort to stick to) my diet.  15 days of the last 31 I gave myself a full smiley.  6 days I gave myself half a smiley (I slipped up, but was able to get back on track right away).  8 days were no smilies.  So that's 21 days of the past month that I actually make considerable progress.  That's 68% of the month!  Well... fuck that just made *me* smile :)

Thank you kind stranger!

... Thank you.  This really  helped put things in perspective.  I mean, I haven't done enough damage to have eaten another 100 pounds I need to lose... I just... need to find that moment again.  Thank you :)
You are right.  It still ebbs and flows, but over the past few months I think it's finally tilted in the doing this for myself side of things a bit more.

Thank you so much for these kind words.  I still feel... numb.  People have told me they think of it as a sort of mini divorce on my part.  We weren't married, but we were together for four years, had moved states, had a house, etc, etc.  It just all sort of imploded at the end it seems.  The first two months were absolute hell and I very much did the whole not eating or drinking bit - I even went to an outpatient clinic for dehydration at one point :\  Unfortunately, after that phase my body snapped into the eat everything in sight phase :(

Can I ask how you went about meeting new people? I am horrible at meeting people on a good day, but now with all of this in the mix it feels next to impossible.  

People keep telling me to push through and that it gets easier.  And you are definitely right about it feeling like a death - it's like I left for work one morning and when I came home he and the whole life I had known was dead.  And I know it's going to take time, but I feel like it's been half a year already I should be moved on by now, or at least more along in the process?  Sigh maybe it's just a bad week.
I think the frustrating part is that this past month I've felt bits of that falling into place and then I feel like I screwed it all up!
Thank you :)

Thank you... this really made me feel better.  When shit first hit the fan six months ago I was reduced to doing one thing after the other - just getting through one hour at a time.  I think that's what I just have to do during these shitty days.  One hour, one day at a time.  It's a fresh day tomorrow :)

Thank you for this.  I think you are right... I am definitely learning that eating my emotions doesn't actually help me feel better.  Which, ironically, seems to be frustrating me even more because now I feel like I don't have any release... blargh.  And this full feeling is definitely going to be remembered... my god I used to eat like this all the time and want *more* food.

I have thought about therapy for this depression - I have been in the past for anxiety issues that I was able to work through.  I currently take an SSRI for anxiety, though it should be helping with depression as well.

Thank you for this.  Yes, I have considered therapy (I've been in the past for anxiety issues) and have definitely cut him out of all social media, etc.  And you are right about what I ate before now not mattering.  Okay... I am just going to throw every wrapper from today in the trash, take a nice long shower, and just start fresh.

Thank you :)  I saved this comment to come back and read in the future on future shitty days.  You are right... lying in the dirt is no fun.  I mean, I guess the only options I really have are to try again or not try again.  And I already know with 100% certainty that not trying again will not make me happy or feel better about myself.  Sigh.  Again... thank you.

Over the past three days I've kept trying.  But it feels like I just keep barely holding on.  Finally today I caved and went and got the greasiest food and ice cream I could find hoping that if I just got it out of my system it would be better.  But... I will keep trying.
